publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Independently reviewed by a second agent; not human-approved.

handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 61r, 61v was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first pass of all 46 manuscript verses. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. There are 92 annotation rows for 46 distinct verses. The two rectangle sets differ in position or dimensions for many verses while retaining the same page per verse. Select the last existing row per line and inspect each exact selected crop as well as its source page. Every selected region encloses the assigned verse; some include neighbouring lines or extra margin. In particular the narrower line-40 rectangle still includes the complete ending anus. witness=Y, sourceWitness=LL and panelId=viewer-panel are navigation provenance only, not a source for readings. Original annotations are unchanged.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. Even lines are indented; lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: Notes are a first-reader evidence queue for a separate reviewer. Observations describe supported features; uncertainty records image limitations; review identifies consequential uncertain interventions. A separate image review has now resolved supported readings and retained local uncertainty; dispositions are recorded in the accompanying ledger.

revisionDesc.change: Independently checked all 46 source verses and all first-pass notes; corrected supported letters, cancellations, ligatures, marks and punctuation. Local uncertainty remains documented; no human scholarly approval is claimed.
First source pass covering all 46 verses and visible interventions in folios 61r, 61v; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: A large decorated N begins the poem and extends beside the first couplet. The source reading submissit is retained. Et ligatures throughout are represented schematically with explicit expansions.
The b of creberrimus, initial i of ilice and u of lucus are darker. All remain legible; no earlier letters or separate hands are inferred.
The eo ending of gramineo is darker; the word remains legible.

A small brown e-like loop lies between arbor and the dark a-like ending. Both are retained locally as uncertain, giving tentative arborea rather than omitting that intervening trace. The initial s of sed is dark. No erased earlier reading is reconstructed.
The source reads tunc cum, with a visible n before c, rather than tum cum.

The baseline reads sumpsit; spumis and three dots appear in the right margin. Both inscriptions remain, without assuming an exact substitution or cancellation sequence. The stridentibus ending and the final et ligature of albet are explicitly encoded.

The m after sua is visibly crossed through horizontally and is encoded as deletion. The initial C is dark; the fine initial h of humum is legible on enlargement. The source retains tenerum and pressit. No text is supplied from another witness. The visible terminal point is retained.
The source word after iterum reads facto, which is preserved without normalization.
The complete verse reads Visus erat somno uires adimente ferenti. Two dots stand in the left margin at this verse level; their function is not established.
The word is disposuisse in the photograph; no normalized substitute is used. The visible terminal point is retained.
The final a of delapsa is darker. The source remains legible.

After garrula a brown t-like ending is crossed by a dark vertical stroke and has a dark point below. It is retained as a canceled uncertain t, rather than rendered as modern exclamation punctuation. The following word reads sedet. The pair of oblique strokes in the right margin remains without an assigned function.
The source clearly reads uobis niueo. Three dots occur in the left margin at this verse level; they are recorded without asserting a textual or correction function.
The b of albentes is darker. The et sign is encoded with its expansion.
The final t of reliquit is darker. Small accent-like strokes above the middle of the line do not securely establish additional letters. The visible terminal point is retained.
Sed nihil is clearly written and retained. The u in liuor is darker; no earlier reading is recoverable from that ink difference.
The o of tauros is dark. A separate oblique stroke follows the verse; it is encoded as a mark of unknown function.
The full verse Carpebant tauri pabula laeta procul is clearly present at this physical position.
A small stain crosses the beginning of fertilioris. Fert is retained tentatively and the remaining ilioris is clear. Herbe preserves the source spelling. The visible terminal point is retained.
The baseline o of augor has a clear dark deletion dot directly beneath it and a dark u above. The two are encoded as an underdotted substitution. The remaining verse is legible.

The baseline reads Sic ergo nocturne sic dixit imaginis augur. A fine dark stroke crosses the initial e of ergo and ends in a point below; a dark loop and fine trailing stroke touch the final e of nocturne. These visible marks are retained schematically without claiming recovered replacement letters or a secure function. The point after ergo is retained.
Quem tu mobilibus foliis uitare uolebas is the complete visible source verse. It is not replaced with a different version of this physical position.
The uit sequence of uitabas and t of estus are darker; no erased earlier reading is claimed. Estus retains the source spelling.
The main line reads Tu uir and compare, with the final e visibly present. The final s of eras is darker. These source forms are preserved. The visible terminal point is retained.

The e of lęna has a visible descending cauda, now retained. The selected last annotation rectangle encloses the complete verse, including anus and the terminal point. The visible terminal point is retained.
Inuiduo is the source sequence and is not normalized. Destituere and the final toro remain legible. The visible terminal point is retained.
Two vertically separated points and a wavy separator follow meos. Both are retained. The decorated A below begins the next poem and is outside this transcription.
The final et of iacet is a ligature, followed by a separate et sign; both are encoded explicitly.
A short dark oblique stroke follows rapuit; its function is not established. The complete source wording remains intact.
A fine oblique stroke follows reliquit; its function is uncertain. No additional letters are supplied.
